newsitem.title: MEXICO: FOCUS-Penoles mining capacity said on rise.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Penoles mining capacity said on rise.

text.p: Mexico's Industrias Penoles, the world's largest silver producer, plans to follow a lackluster 1996 with aggressive precious-metal production beginning in 1997, analysts said Monday.

Depressed world gold and silver prices in 1996 contributed to lower net earnings for the company. Earnings per share fell to 2.72 pesos, down from 3.17 pesos in 1995, and net earnings fell to 1.101 billion pesos from 1.291 billion pesos in 1995.
Silver processed from the company's own mines will rise to 59 percent of Penoles's total, up from 52 percent, while lead will remain at 38 percent, the company said.

Penoles plans a 101-percent production increase in gold and a 70-percent increase in zinc output in the following four years, the company said in a report obtained on Monday by Reuters. Silver output will rise 18 percent and lead will rise 10 percent, the report said.
"If sustained over the year, the rise in zinc prices in 1997 is worth nine percent of Penoles's annual profit, while the fall in gold prices is only three percent," Bodenberg told Reuters.
A weaker peso and strong demand for the company's growing zinc production should also encourage improved 1997 earnings, Chris Albi of Valores Finamex in Mexico City told Reuters.
Silver accounts for about 35 percent of the company's sales and zinc makes up about 17 percent of sales.
The company's 1997 results will depend on the trend in world metal prices, Santander Investment analyst Sandra Morfin said.

Bodenberg said he projected 1997 earnings per share to rise to 3.25 pesos, above 1995 levels, because of the expected recovery in world prices for precious metals and early fruits of long-term production expansion.

Although the company's share price has rebounded to 37 pesos from about 26 pesos at the beginning of the year, Bodenberg said the shares are still attractive because of long-term growth expectations due to the greater percentage of production from Penoles's own mines.
The company's shares closed up 1.85 pesos to 38.35 pesos on Monday, close to a year high of 38.60 pesos.
Analysts said further information on the company will be available in the company's first-ever conference call with analysts on Tuesday.
